mechanism_narrative: A continuing recovery in workplaces mobility reduces workday drag and lifts retail visits within four weeks. If WORKPLACES keeps edging up while TRANSIT stays less depressed, RETAIL_REC should rise relative to the prior four-week average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed its last-4-week mean after four weeks despite WORKPLACES rising or holding above -16% and TRANSIT improving from its current level.

mechanism_narrative: When residential mobility falls from its elevated level, discretionary out-of-home time expands and retail-recreation mobility rises over the next two weeks. The signal is strongest if RESIDENTIAL stops trending down and RETAIL_REC has already been improving week to week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls at least 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: A week-on-week drop in RESIDENTIAL is followed by no upward move in RETAIL_REC within two weeks in a majority of observed cases.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between transit recovery and workplace recovery increases retail traffic only when both improve together. If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both move higher for several weeks, the combined commute-and-errand effect should push RETAIL_REC upward within four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise over four weeks when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve simultaneously, or rises when only one of them improves at a time.

mechanism_narrative: A constrained transit environment suppresses retail visits because fewer commuting and transfer trips create fewer incidental shopping opportunities. If TRANSIT remains more than 20 points below baseline, RETAIL_REC should stay below its recent average over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -20 for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean despite TRANSIT remaining below -20 for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in parks mobility diverts discretionary outings toward outdoor recreation, reducing the share of trips going to retail and recreation over the next week. If PARKS keeps strengthening from a negative to positive weekly level, RETAIL_REC should soften immediately.
candidate_trigger: PARKS crosses above 0 after being negative
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not decline within one week after PARKS crosses above zero from a previously negative reading.

mechanism_narrative: Retail mobility keeps rising only if grocery-and-pharmacy trips plateau while residential time stops absorbing most activities. A sustained increase in GROCERY_PHARM combined with stable or falling RESIDENTIAL indicates a broadening of errand-based movement that lifts RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains flat or falls over four weeks even as GROCERY_PHARM stays elevated and RESIDENTIAL stops increasing.

mechanism_narrative: In a restriction-easing regime, rising workplace and transit mobility translate into higher retail-recreation mobility because commuting and discretionary trips are reconnected. The effect should appear within two weeks only when both proxies are above their prior-week levels.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both increase week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within two weeks after simultaneous week-on-week gains in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: The current pattern of low transit and negative workplaces mobility signals weak weekday circulation that continues to cap retail activity. If this pattern persists, RETAIL_REC should remain below its last four-week mean over the next four weeks rather than continue its recent gradual recovery.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC exceeds its last-4-week average over the next four weeks while TRANSIT remains near -22 and WORKPLACES remains around -15 or lower.
